OSHA 1910.269 (and 1926 Subpart V for construction) limits work near energized lines to qualified electrical employees, with minimum approach distances. Gas or water crews cannot legally substitute for line crews on energized work.

Under the ANSI/NETA ETT-based certification, only Level III and IV technicians are considered fully certified to perform and supervise electrical testing (substation/switchyard). This is the scarce credential shared between T&D substation and power-gen switchyard work.

Union gas distribution work runs under a National Distribution Pipeline Agreement between the Distribution Contractors Association and the United Association (UA), separate from IBEW outside line agreements. Union jurisdiction follows the trade.

49 CFR 192.723 requires gas distribution leak surveys at least once each calendar year (at intervals of no more than 15 months) in business districts, and at least once every 5 calendar years (no more than 63 months) outside them.
